references.text: Moses commands the Levites to kill those who had sinned with the golden calf, a similar example of how Israel's leaders had to carry out judgment on idolaters.
The law requires that those who lead others into idolatry be put to death, even if they are close family members.
Moses reminds Israel that the Lord wiped out all who followed Baal-Peor, while those who held fast to the Lord were spared.
Reference to the sin at Peor as a warning about the consequences of unfaithfulness to the Lord.
The psalmist describes how Israel bound themselves to Baal-Peor and ate sacrifices offered to dead gods, which led to a plague.
Israel killed the Midianite kings and Balaam as punishment for leading Israel into sin at Peor.
Hosea mentions Baal-Peor as an example of Israel's early apostasy and shame.
